title: Genghis Khan
subtitle: From outcast to world conqueror, 1162 to 1279

steps.title: A boy on the Onon
steps.text: Temujin was born around 1162 near the Onon River, in what is now northeastern Mongolia. When he was about eight, his father Yesugei was poisoned by Tatars, and the clan abandoned the widow and her children. The family survived by hunting, fishing and gathering. As a youth he was taken captive by a rival clan and escaped.

steps.title: Khan of all the Mongols
steps.text: After years of shifting alliances and wars, Temujin broke the Kereit and, in 1204, the Naimans. In 1206 an assembly at the source of the Onon River proclaimed him Genghis Khan, ruler of the united steppe tribes. The meaning of the title is still debated.

steps.title: The first campaign beyond the steppe
steps.text: The first target outside the steppe was the kingdom of Western Xia. In 1209 Genghis led his army south to its capital Zhongxing, modern Yinchuan. The Mongols lacked siege equipment, and in January 1210 a dam on the Yellow River broke and flooded their own camp. Even so, the Xia emperor submitted and paid tribute.

steps.title: The fall of Zhongdu
steps.text: In 1211 Genghis turned on the Jin dynasty, which ruled northern China. His army won in the field at Huan'erzhui and ravaged the north. Zhongdu, the Jin capital on the site of modern Beijing, was besieged and then spared when peace was made in 1214. The peace did not hold. Zhongdu surrendered on 31 May 1215 and was sacked.

steps.title: The caravan at Otrar
steps.text: In 1218 the governor of Otrar, a frontier city of the Khwarazmian shah, massacred a Mongol caravan of about 450 merchants and seized its goods. The shah then killed a Mongol envoy. Genghis invaded in 1219. Otrar fell in February 1220, Bukhara the same month after a march across the Kyzylkum Desert, and Samarkand in March.

steps.title: Jalal al-Din at the Indus
steps.text: Shah Muhammad died a fugitive on an island in the Caspian Sea. His son Jalal al-Din fought on and beat a Mongol army at Parwan in September 1221. Genghis caught him on the bank of the Indus on 24 November and destroyed his army. Jalal al-Din is said to have ridden his horse off a cliff into the river, and he escaped into India.
steps.artCaption: Jalal ad-Din crossing the Indus, escaping Genghis Khan

steps.title: The great raid
steps.text: After the shah's death the generals Jebe and Subutai rode on, a raid of some 7,500 kilometres around the Caspian Sea. They crossed Persia and Georgia, passed the Caucasus at Derbent, and on 31 May 1223 destroyed an army of Rus princes and Cumans on the Kalka River, in what is now eastern Ukraine. Then they turned back east.

steps.title: Death in Western Xia
steps.text: Genghis returned to subdue a rebellious Western Xia. He died in August 1227 while the siege of its capital was still under way. The cause is unknown: sources name illness, an arrow wound and even lightning. His death was kept secret. He was buried on or near the mountain Burkhan Khaldun, and the site of the grave is not known.

steps.title: Mohi
steps.text: Under his son Ogedei, crowned khan in 1229, the armies went west again. On 11 April 1241 Batu and Subutai destroyed the Hungarian army on the Sajo River at Mohi, two days after another Mongol force won at Legnica. King Bela IV fled to the Adriatic coast. Hungary is estimated to have lost 15 to 25 percent of its people.

steps.title: The fall of Baghdad
steps.text: The Mongol prince Hulagu led an army against the Abbasid caliph. The assault on Baghdad began at the end of January 1258 and the city surrendered on 10 February. A week of killing and looting followed. Caliph al-Mustasim was executed on 20 February, reportedly rolled in a carpet and trampled by horses so that no royal blood was spilled.

steps.title: Kublai and the Great Yuan
steps.text: Kublai, a grandson of Genghis, was proclaimed Great Khan in 1260 and fought his brother Ariq Boke for the title until 1264. That civil war began the division of the empire. In 1271 Kublai gave his realm a Chinese dynastic name, Great Yuan, and the next year he made Dadu, modern Beijing, his capital.
steps.artCaption: Kublai Khan, Yuan imperial portrait album

steps.title: The last of the Song
steps.text: Kublai's armies wore down southern China. Xiangyang fell in 1273 and the Song court surrendered in 1276. On 19 March 1279 a Yuan fleet crushed the last loyalists at Yamen, on the coast of Guangdong, and a minister leapt into the sea with the seven year old emperor. Kublai was the first ruler from outside the Han people to hold all of China.
